topic: Problem 5.6: uniqueness of finite products of m!/m^m for distinct integer parameters greater than one
title: Equal products of m!/m^m over distinct parameter sets

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We answer Problem 5.6 of Aivazidis, Loukaki and Müller in the negative (J. Group Theory 27 (2024), p. 1281): the product of the weights f(m)=m!/m^m does not determine a finite set of distinct integers greater than one. The same example answers arXiv:2209.00986v1, Problem 12.6, and v2, Problem 5.6. The two disjoint eighteen-element sets have equal products and equal parameter sums. Their equality follows from the adjacent-weight identity f(n+1)/f(n)=(n/(n+1))^n and an explicit prime-exponent table. For every cardinality at least nineteen, infinitely many rational values have two distinct representations with equal cardinalities and equal sums.
summary: Ma and Zhang give a prime-exponent proof answering Problem 5.6 and its original arXiv v1 Problem 12.6 negatively. Written corollaries give equal-sum examples at every cardinality at least eighteen, infinitely many multiply represented values at each cardinality at least nineteen, and uniqueness for coordinatewise-comparable parameter lists. A source-item table distinguishes other group-theoretic questions and the prior prime-side theorem.
